flags.evidence: Opened page/index.html from disk in Chromium at 1440x900 (DSF 1) and 390x844 (DSF 3); no script errors. Scrolled to the section 'How a week gets planned'. At both widths the first step (li > h3 'Take stock', visible 17px paragraph) reads: 'Tap what's in the fridge, the cupboard and the freezer. It takes about a minute the first time, and Pantrywise remembers it between weeks.' This is a usage/performance time figure stated as typical fact. The brief supplies no timing or usage data and says there are no users yet, so the figure is not a brief fact. It is not inside the labelled demo: the only 'example' label ('These are example dinners to show how the planning works...') sits in the fridge demo in the hero, not next to this step at either width. It is also not a plain status statement. It matches the table's own example of a performance claim stated as typical ('scans in under a second'), so it meets HF2. (The 'thirty minutes or under' recipe lines describe how the company writes its own dinners, so they are a product spec, not proof; the confirmation rests on the 'about a minute' claim.)
